title: Input call machine
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean words, let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input $x$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $C$, entry and exit states of $C$, and a natural number $c$ with at least one work tape, such that for every input $x$, starting from the clean seam in the entry state with all work tapes blank, there is a positive time $t\\le c(T(|x|)+|x|+|f(x)|+1)$ at which $C$ reaches the clean seam in the exit state with $f(x)$ on its first work tape and all other work tapes blank; the exit state is not visited at any earlier positive time before $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean words
$f$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$M$ computes $f$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every input $x$
